# API Mapping Logic Inventory

This inventory covers mapping logic found under `mesx-master-api/src`. It focuses on code that shapes entities, raw query results, or request payloads into API response DTOs or persistence payloads.

## ISA-95 Material Definition

File: `modules/isa95-material-model/material/helpers/material.mapper.ts`

### `MaterialDefinitionMapper.toResponseDto(materialDefinition, languageCode = 'EN')`

Maps a `MaterialDefinition` entity into `MaterialDefinitionResponseDto`.

It maps:

- assigned material classes into `{ id, code, description }`
- material properties into response property DTOs
- material descriptions into the preferred language
- storage locations from the `storageLocations` property

Important logic:

- `findDescriptionByLanguage(...)` uses the shared language helper to pick the best description.
- `mapPropertyDescriptions(...)` builds `valueDescriptions` for JSON property keys.
- `normalizePropertyKey(...)` removes non-alphanumeric characters and lowercases keys so values like `specialProcurement` and class property codes can match.

Used by:

- `modules/isa95-material-model/material/material.service.ts`
  - `findAll(...)`
  - `findOne(...)`
  - `syncMaterialClasses(...)` indirectly through `findOne(...)`

## ISA-95 Material Definition Service

File: `modules/isa95-material-model/material/material.service.ts`

### `findAll(...)`

Loads material definitions with all needed relations and maps every entity with:

```ts
MaterialDefinitionMapper.toResponseDto(item, languageCode)
```

Returns a paginated object:

- `items`
- `limit`
- `page`
- `total`

### `findOne(...)`

Loads one material definition and maps it with:

```ts
MaterialDefinitionMapper.toResponseDto(materialDefinition)
```

### `getSuggestions(...)`

Uses raw query aliases to return `MaterialDefinitionSuggestionDto` rows:

- `code`
- `description`

The description is selected with SQL `COALESCE` between requested language and English fallback.

### `syncMaterialClasses(...)`

Contains request-side mapping logic:

- deduplicates `materialClassIds`
- merges incoming `properties` by `materialClassId`
- maps missing class relations into `MaterialMaterialClass` entities
- maps property input values into `MaterialProperty` entities
- merges new JSON values into existing `propertiesJson`

## ISA-95 Material Class

File: `modules/isa95-material-model/material-class/material-class.service.ts`

### `MaterialClassService.toResponseDto(materialClass, languageCode = 'EN')`

Maps a `MaterialClass` entity into `MaterialClassResponseDto`.

Fields mapped:

- `id`
- `code`
- `description`
- `isCustom`
- `languageCode`
- `materialClassPropertiesCount`

Description behavior:

- selects the preferred language through `findPreferredDescription`
- resolves the actual language code through `resolveDescriptionLanguageCode`
- falls back to an empty description when none is found

Used by:

- `create(...)`
- `findAll(...)`
- `findOne(...)`
- `update(...)`

### `MaterialClassService.mapMaterialForClass(...)`

Maps a `MaterialDefinition` linked to a class into `MaterialClassRelatedMaterialDto`.

Fields mapped:

- `id`
- `code`
- `description`
- `descriptionLanguageCode`
- `plant`
- `properties`

It filters `materialProperties` to only the selected `materialClassId`, sorts by property id, and maps each property to:

- `id`
- `materialClassId`
- `propertiesJson`

Used by:

- `findRelatedMaterials(...)`

### `findRelatedMaterials(...)`

Maps material-class links into unique related materials:

- loads `MaterialMaterialClass` links
- deduplicates by material definition id
- maps each material through `mapMaterialForClass(...)`

## Shared Language Mapping Helpers

File: `modules/isa95-material-model/shared/helpers/language-description.helper.ts`

### `normalizeLanguageCode(languageCode?)`

Trims and uppercases language codes.

Falls back to `EN`.

### `findPreferredDescription(descriptions, languageCode?)`

Chooses the best description in this order:

- requested language
- English fallback, when requested language is not English
- first available description

### `resolveDescriptionLanguageCode(description, requestedLanguageCode?)`

Returns the actual selected description language, or the normalized requested language when no description exists.

These helpers are used by the material definition and material class mapping logic.

## BOM Mapping

File: `modules/bom/utils/bom-service.utility.ts`

### `BOMServiceUtility.transformComponentToResponseDTO(component)`

Maps a `BOMComponent` entity into `BOMComponentResponseDTO`.

Fields mapped:

- `component` from `materialId`
- `materialCategory`
- `id`
- `itemNumber` from `positionNr`, padded to four digits
- `kitmat`, defaulting to `false`
- `quantity`
- `skipBomLevel`, defaulting to `false`
- `subComponents`, defaulting to `[]`
- `uom` from `unitOfMeasure`

### `BOMServiceUtility.buildNestedComponentsResponse(...)`

Maps BOM components recursively into nested `BOMComponentResponseDTO` arrays.

Important logic:

- maps each component through `transformComponentToResponseDTO(...)`
- adds nested `subComponents` when the component has its own BOM
- tracks processed BOM numbers to avoid cycles

### `BOMServiceUtility.createBaseBOMResponse(bom)`

Maps a `BOM` entity into a base `BOMResponseDTO`:

- `erpBomId`
- `validFrom`
- `validTo`
- `components: []`

File: `modules/bom/bom.service.ts`

### `buildBOMResponseWithNestedComponents(...)`

Builds a complete `BOMResponseDTO` with nested component mapping.

Important logic:

- creates the root BOM response from `bomNumber`, `validFrom`, and `validTo`
- maps component entities through `BOMServiceUtility.transformComponentToResponseDTO(...)`
- enriches components with `componentType` from the material table
- maps nested component responses while preserving selected fields

### `getBOMsByBomId(...)`

Maps matching BOM entities into a `GetBOMsResponseDTO`.

Each BOM row is mapped to:

- `erpBomId`
- `materialId`
- `validFrom`
- `validTo`

## Seeding Mapping

Files under `seeding/core` also contain mapping logic, especially:

- `seeding/core/seed-discovery.helper.ts`
- `seeding/core/seed-execution.helper.ts`
- `seeding/core/seed-key.helper.ts`

This mapping is seed/import infrastructure rather than runtime API response mapping. The key function is `mapRowToPayload(...)`, which maps seed source rows into entity payloads according to seed schema mappings.

## Main Takeaway

Yes, `mesx-master-api/src` contains mapping logic. The clearest dedicated mapper is `MaterialDefinitionMapper`, but mapping is also embedded in material class services/DTOs, BOM utilities, storage services, and legacy material services. Most of it is entity-to-response DTO mapping, with some request-to-entity mapping in material definition class sync and material bulk update flows.

# Seeding Guide

This folder contains the seeding system used to insert reference/master data in an idempotent way.

## Current Setup

Seeding is JSON-first and currently uses:

- `src/seeding/run-seed.ts` as CLI entrypoint.
- `src/seeding/core/seed-runner.ts` as generic loader/executor.
- `src/migration.data.source.ts` as shared TypeORM DataSource.

Seed files live under `src/seeding/data/**` with the naming convention `*.seed-data.json`.

## Run Seeding

From project root:

```bash
npm run seed
```

By default, this runs with selector `all`.

Explicit examples:

```bash
npm run seed -- all
npm run seed -- material
npm run seed -- material-classes
```

## Execution Flow

1. `run-seed.ts` reads CLI selectors from `process.argv`.
2. If no selector is provided, selector defaults to `all`.
3. Runner discovers seed files recursively in `src/seeding/data`.
4. It loads each seed definition and resolves `table` to a real entity class.
5. Files are sorted by `order`, then by `id`.
6. Files are filtered by selector (`id` or `tags`).
7. It initializes the shared DataSource (if not already initialized).
8. It runs each selected seed file sequentially.
9. For each file, only missing rows are inserted.

## Seed JSON Format

Each file is a full seed definition object:

```json
{
  "id": "material-classes",
  "order": 10,
  "table": "material-class",
  "tags": ["material"],
  "schema": {
    "inputKeyColumns": ["code"],
    "tableKeyColumns": ["code"],
    "mapping": {
      "code": { "type": "column", "sourceColumn": "code" },
      "description": { "type": "column", "sourceColumn": "description" },
      "isCustom": { "type": "constant", "value": false }
    }
  },
  "data": [
    {
      "code": "GENERAL_MATERIAL_IDENTIFICATION",
      "description": "General Material Identification"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Schema Fields

- `id`: unique seed identifier used for filtering and dependencies.
- `order`: execution order (lower runs first).
- `table`: table key resolved in `seed-runner.ts` (`seedEntityRegistry`).
- `tags`: optional group labels for selector-based runs.
- `data`: source rows.
- `schema.inputKeyColumns`: key used to deduplicate source rows and resolve references.
- `schema.tableKeyColumns`: key used to detect existing DB rows.
- `schema.tableRelationsToLoad`: optional relation names to load for nested keys.
- `schema.mapping`: transformation from source row to entity payload.

## Mapping Types

`mapping` supports three mapping types:

1. `column`
Copies value from source row.
Example: `"description": { "type": "column", "sourceColumn": "propertyName" }`

2. `constant`
Uses a fixed value for all rows.
Example: `"isCustom": { "type": "constant", "value": false }`

3. `reference`
Resolves and injects a related entity from another seed file already processed.
Example:

```json
"materialClass": {
  "type": "reference",
  "dataFileId": "material-classes",
  "keyColumns": ["classCode"]
}
```

For `reference`:

- `dataFileId` points to another seed file `id`.
- `keyColumns` are read from the current source row to build the lookup key.
- The referenced file must run first (lower `order`).

## Idempotency Logic

For each seed file:

1. Source rows are deduplicated by `inputKeyColumns`.
2. Existing DB rows are loaded and indexed by `tableKeyColumns`.
3. Rows already present are skipped.
4. Only missing rows are inserted.
5. Final DB rows are indexed and stored in context for downstream `reference` mappings.

This allows running the same seed multiple times without duplicate inserts.

## Selectors

Supported selector modes:

- `all`: run all discovered seed files.
- `<seed-id>`: run one specific seed file.
- `<tag>`: run all seed files with that tag.

## Add a New Seed

1. Create `src/seeding/data/<domain>/<name>.seed-data.json`.
2. Fill `id`, `order`, `table`, `schema`, and `data`.
3. Add/confirm `table` key in `seedEntityRegistry` inside `src/seeding/core/seed-runner.ts`.
4. If using `reference`, ensure dependency seed has lower `order`.
5. Run `npm run seed -- <id-or-tag>` to validate.

## Troubleshooting

`EntityMetadataNotFoundError` during seed run usually means entity discovery is misconfigured for runtime mode.

Current config supports both `ts-node` and compiled runs in:

- `src/config/database/mssql/configuration.ts`
- `entities: ['src/**/*.entity.ts', 'dist/**/*.entity.js']`

# MESX Master API: AI Project Guide

## Purpose

This project is a NestJS + TypeORM backend for MES/master-data workflows.
It contains two main realities:

1. Active application modules already wired into `AppModule` for existing MES APIs.
2. A newer ISA-95-oriented data model under `src/modules/isa95-*` that appears to be partially implemented and not fully integrated yet.

This guide is written for AI agents so they can orient quickly and avoid making wrong assumptions.

## Tech Stack

- Framework: NestJS 10
- Language: TypeScript
- ORM: TypeORM 0.3
- Database: Microsoft SQL Server
- Messaging/integration: Azure Event Hub, Dapr
- Validation/docs: class-validator, class-transformer, Swagger decorators
- Runtime: Node.js 20

Useful scripts from `package.json`:

- `npm run start:dev`
- `npm run build`
- `npm run test`
- `npm run typeorm:migrate`
- `npm run seed`

## High-Level Project Shape

Main entrypoints:

- `src/main.ts`
- `src/app.module.ts`
- `src/migration.data.source.ts`

Currently wired application modules in `src/app.module.ts` include:

- `material`
- `material-dtl`
- `bom`
- `storage-location`
- `material-storage-location`
- `shift-details`
- `ingestion-event-tracking`
- config/messaging/support modules

Important note for AI agents:

- The ISA-95 controllers/services/entities exist in the codebase.
- They are not imported into the root `AppModule` right now.
- Do not assume the ISA-95 REST endpoints are live unless you verify module wiring first.

## Key Folders

- `src/modules/`
  Core domain modules.
- `src/modules/isa95-material-model/`
  ISA-95 material master model.
- `src/modules/isa95-bom-operations-model/`
  ISA-95 BOM and operation model.
- `src/migration/`
  SQL Server schema evolution.
- `src/seeding/`
  JSON-first idempotent seed system.
- `src/config/`
  App, DB, Event Hub, and integration config.

## What The ISA-95 Part Is Trying To Model

The ISA-95 area is centered around a structured master-data model for:

- material definitions
- multilingual material descriptions
- material classes
- class inheritance
- class properties
- per-material property values
- BOM definitions and BOM items
- operation definitions and operation segments

The schema name used for this area is:

- `isa95`

The initial base tables were created in:

- [1773501000000-create-master-data-tables.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/migration/1773501000000-create-master-data-tables.ts:1)

Material-model expansion came later in:

- [1774883159122-create-material-data-model.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/migration/1774883159122-create-material-data-model.ts:1)
- [1775904000000-rename-material-class-parent-to-inheritance.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/migration/1775904000000-rename-material-class-parent-to-inheritance.ts:1)
- [1776358204355-fix-material-data-model.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/migration/1776358204355-fix-material-data-model.ts:1)

## ISA-95 Core Entities

### 1. Material Definition

File:

- [material-definition.entity.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/modules/isa95-material-model/material-definition/material-definition.entity.ts:1)

Represents the core material identity per plant.

Main fields:

- `plant`
- `id`
- `code`
- `erpSource`

Important relationships:

- one material definition -> many descriptions by language
- one material definition -> many material/class assignments
- one material definition -> many material properties
- one material definition -> many BOM definitions
- one material definition -> many BOM items
- one material definition -> many operation definitions

Important observation:

- Older migrations created a `code` column intended for language code.
- A later migration removed that column.
- So the current model no longer stores an explicit language code in this table even though the table name still says "by language".

This is important for any AI work touching multilingual behavior: the naming and the current schema do not fully match.

## Current State Of ISA APIs

There are CRUD-style controllers/services for:

- material definition
- material class
- material/material-class links

Examples:

- [material-definition.controller.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/modules/isa95-material-model/material-definition/material-definition.controller.ts:1)
- [material-class.controller.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/modules/isa95-material-model/material-class/material-class.controller.ts:1)
- [material-material-class.controller.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/modules/isa95-material-model/material-material-class/material-material-class.controller.ts:1)

But AI agents should be careful:

- these controllers are not clearly registered through complete feature modules
- some feature modules only register entities, not controllers/services
- the root `AppModule` does not import ISA modules

So the code contains endpoint definitions, but application wiring appears incomplete.

## Important Inconsistencies And Risks

These are the main traps for future AI/code work:

### 1. DTOs do not fully match current entities

Example:

- `CreateMaterialClassDto` still has `description`
- `MaterialClass` entity now uses `code` and no longer has `description`

Files:

- [create-material-class.dto.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/modules/isa95-material-model/material-class/dtos/create-material-class.dto.ts:1)
- [material-class.entity.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/modules/isa95-material-model/material-class/material-class.entity.ts:1)

This suggests the ISA95 CRUD layer has not been fully updated after schema changes.

### 2. Migration history and current entity names diverged

The schema evolved from `site` to `plant` and removed some columns. AI agents should always inspect the latest entity plus latest migrations, not just the earliest migration.

### 3. “By language” naming no longer guarantees language storage

`material_description_by_language` currently lacks a language-code column in the entity and latest migration state.

### 4. Some modules are skeletal

Example:

- `MaterialClassModule` imports the entity repository but does not declare controller/provider wiring.

Files:

- [material-class.module.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/modules/isa95-material-model/material-class/material-class.module.ts:1)
- [material-class-property.module.ts](/home/melkifir/mesx-master-api/src/modules/isa95-material-model/material-class-property/material-class-property.module.ts:1)

### 5. Material-material-class link handling may be incomplete

The link entity includes `plant`, but the create service builds the link mainly from found entities and may not fully align with the entity shape or DB constraints. Verify behavior before extending it.

## Recommended Mental Model For AI Agents

When working in the ISA part, think in three layers:

1. Identity layer
   `MaterialDefinition`

2. Classification/schema layer
   `MaterialClass`, `MaterialClassInheritance`, `MaterialClassProperty`, `PropertyDataType`

3. Instance/value/execution layer
   `MaterialProperty`, `BOMDefinition`, `BOMItems`, `OperationDefinition`, `OperationSegment`

Also remember:

- `plant` is part of identity for several ISA tables
- JSON fields are used to carry flexible semantics and property values
- migrations are the source of truth for real schema evolution
- seed files are the best source of business intent for material classes/properties

## Good Starting Points For Future Work

If an AI agent needs to continue ISA95 work, start here:

1. Verify whether ISA modules should be exposed in `AppModule`.
2. Reconcile DTOs, controllers, services, and entities after recent schema changes.
3. Decide whether `material_description_by_language` should actually store a language code again.
4. Add tests around material class creation, class-property creation, and material/class linking.
5. Use the seed files as the baseline taxonomy rather than inventing new class/property names.

## Short Summary

This repository is an MES master-data API with a partially integrated ISA-95 domain model. The ISA section is valuable and fairly rich at the entity/migration level, especially for material classification and BOM/operation structures, but it is not yet fully aligned at the module, DTO, and runtime-wiring levels. Any AI agent working here should treat the ISA95 area as real but still under construction.

# Operation Segment APIs – Change Notes (for Handover)

## Scope
This note summarizes the latest aligned behavior for these 2 APIs in `v1/isa95-operation-model/operation-segments`:

1. `GET /isa95-operation-model/operation-segments`
2. `GET /isa95-operation-model/operation-segments/by-material`

Goal of the change: make `by-material` follow the same filtering and response format pattern as the main operation-segments API (except `WHERE` clause target).

---

## 1) `GET /operation-segments` (by operation definition)

### Query DTO
- `plant: number` (required)
- `operationDefinitionId: number` (required)
- `status?: 'All' | 'Active' | 'Inactive'` (optional, default `All`)

### Filtering
- Base filters:
  - `os.plant = :plant`
  - `od.id = :operationDefinitionId`
- Status filter:
  - `Active`: `od.effectiveStartDate <= today AND od.effectiveEndDate >= today`
  - `Inactive`: `od.effectiveStartDate > today OR od.effectiveEndDate < today`
  - `All`: no additional status date filter

### Response format
- Type: `WrappedResponse<Array<GroupedOperationSegmentsResultDto> | undefined>`
- Grouping key:
  - `materialCode`
  - `groupCounter`
  - `taskGroupId`
  - `effectiveStartDate` (ISO)
- Each row includes computed `status: 'Active' | 'Inactive'`.

---

## 2) `GET /operation-segments/by-material` (by material)

### What changed
This API was converted to match API #1 behavior/style.

### Query DTO (current)
- `plant: number` (required)
- `material: string` (required)
- `status?: 'All' | 'Active' | 'Inactive'` (optional, default `All`)

### Removed from query DTO
- `limit`
- `page`

### Filtering
- Base filters:
  - `m.plant = :plant`
  - `m.code = :material` where material is normalized with `.trim()`
- Status filter: same logic as API #1
  - `Active`: `od.effectiveStartDate <= today AND od.effectiveEndDate >= today`
  - `Inactive`: `od.effectiveStartDate > today OR od.effectiveEndDate < today`

### Response format (current)
- Type: `WrappedResponse<Array<GroupedOperationSegmentsResultDto> | undefined>`
- Grouping strategy: same as API #1 (`materialCode + groupCounter + taskGroupId + effectiveStartDate`)
- Row shape: same projection used by API #1 (`OperationSegmentTableRowDto` fields + computed `status`)

### Removed from response
- No pagination object anymore:
  - removed `total`
  - removed `limit`
  - removed `page`

---

## Controller / Swagger alignment
`operation-segment.controller.ts` was updated so `by-material` now documents:

- optional `status` query (`All | Active | Inactive`)
- grouped response example (same structure as the main API)
- return type aligned to grouped array response

---

## Files impacted
- `src/modules/isa95-bom-operations-model/operation-segment/operation-segment.service.ts`
- `src/modules/isa95-bom-operations-model/operation-segment/operation-segment.controller.ts`
- `src/modules/isa95-bom-operations-model/operation-segment/dtos/get-operation-segments-by-material.dto.ts`

---

## Notes for next agent
- `by-material` and `by-operationDefinitionId` now share the same output contract and grouping semantics.
- The only intended functional difference is the base `WHERE` target:
  - API #1 uses operation definition id.
  - API #2 uses material code.
- If any consumer still expects pagination fields on `by-material`, that consumer must be updated.
